description: Consumers who pay per printed product, about 80 percent in the United States, then Australia, Europe and the UK; this part covers the Facebook Timeline Archivist and the Seasonal Gift Giver.

customers.name: Facebook Timeline Archivist
customers.description: Someone in their fifties or sixties, most often in the United States or Australia, who has lived 10 to 15 years of family life on Facebook: albums from holidays and birthdays, timeline pictures friends tagged, mobile uploads from the phone and a decade of cover and profile photos. Uses the Facebook Photo Books flow on pastbook.com rather than the app, logs in with Facebook, picks a single year between 2009 and 2025 and expects the book to arrive with the original captions and dates so that "my 2016" reads like a diary. Less technical and price-sensitive: the small hardcover at USD 19.99 for 24 pages is the default, the large 12" x 8.5" format is for a special year, and a promo code usually decides when the next year gets ordered. Used to print Instagram years too and was cut off when Instagram discontinued third-party access for personal accounts, so trust that Facebook stays available and that photos are handled privately weighs as much as price.
careAbout: One click from Facebook Login to a finished book of a whole year, with the captions and dates Facebook already holds carried onto the pages
A free preview before paying, because the small hardcover at USD 19.99 is bought on a fixed income and the page count decides the price
Clear, plain-language explanation of what PastBook takes from Facebook, that photos travel over encrypted connections and that nothing is kept longer than the order needs
Every year from 2009 to 2025 available so that the shelf can be completed year by year, in the same size and cover so the spines line up
Books that print the grandchildren's faces sharply from Facebook-sized photos, without blurry duplicates the AI should have dropped
Support that answers by e-mail or WhatsApp without jargon when Facebook Login asks for a permission they do not understand
winsThem: The Facebook Photo Books page that shows the book of a year being built from albums, timeline pictures, cover and profile photos while they watch
Trustpilot 4.5 from 35,837 reviews with 79 percent five-star, and a reply from PastBook under every negative review, which reads as a company that answers
A discount code or free hardcover upgrade in the Year in Review campaign that turns "one day" into "order 2016 tonight"
A help center article that explains the Facebook permission screen step by step and the honest notice about Instagram ending support for photo products
The first book arriving within the published US window of 4 to 8 business days with the captions exactly as they were written years ago
theirFear: Granting Facebook Login and discovering that PastBook, or Meta, has more of their photos than they meant to share, or that the connection breaks as Instagram did
Paying for a book whose captions are missing, whose photos are low-resolution or whose pages are padded with near-duplicates, and having nobody to call
Losing the Facebook years altogether if the account is closed or the photos are gone before they are printed

jobsToBeDone.name: Print a whole Facebook year with captions in one click
jobsToBeDone.whatItIs: Turn one calendar year of a Facebook life, spread over albums, timeline pictures, cover and profile photos and mobile uploads, into a printed hardcover without selecting photos or designing pages. The job includes granting Facebook Login, picking the year, letting the curation engine drop duplicates and blurry shots while keeping the captions and dates, checking the free preview and paying for a book that matches the years already on the shelf.
jobsToBeDone.outcome: A finished hardcover of the chosen year, with captions and dates preserved and no duplicate or blurry photos, previewed for free in under a minute, ordered at a price the archivist understood before checkout and delivered within the published window for their country.

steps.step: Log in with Facebook and understand the permission screen
steps.description: On pastbook.com the archivist opens Facebook Photo Books, signs in with Facebook and is asked which photo permissions to grant. The step succeeds when the permission request is explained in plain words, covers albums, timeline pictures, cover and profile photos and mobile uploads within the scope Meta allows, and the archivist knows the photos are imported over an encrypted connection.

streamsNeeded.name: Protect Photo Privacy And Platform Compliance

steps.step: Pick the year to print
steps.description: Photos are grouped per year from 2009 to 2025 and the archivist chooses the one that is missing from the shelf, sees how many photos it holds and whether it is a thin year that will fit the 24-page small hardcover or a rich year that will run to 60 pages.

streamsNeeded.name: Connect Facebook And Pick A Year

steps.step: Let the engine choose the best photos and keep the captions
steps.description: The curation engine scores quality, removes duplicates and blurry shots and groups the year into moments in under 60 seconds. For a Facebook year the captions and posting dates are the point of the book, so they must survive selection and land next to the photo they belonged to.

streamsNeeded.name: Curate The Best Photos With Ai
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Analyses image quality and context, removes duplicates and near-duplicates and groups the year into moments while keeping the Facebook captions attached.

streamsNeeded.name: Auto Design The Book And Preview
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Lays out the moments with the captions and dates as page text and produces the free preview in under a minute.

jobsToBeDone.name: Keep my photos safe and private while the book is made
jobsToBeDone.whatItIs: Be certain that connecting Facebook to PastBook does not expose family photos, including grandchildren, to anyone beyond the print job. The job covers understanding the permission screen, knowing where the photos go and for how long, being able to disconnect and delete, and getting a human answer when a permission request or a platform change such as the end of Instagram support raises doubts.
jobsToBeDone.outcome: The archivist connects Facebook knowing exactly which photos are read and why, the photos are transferred and stored encrypted only for as long as the order needs, disconnection and deletion work on request within the legal deadlines, and no privacy question stays unanswered for more than a day.

steps.step: Understand what is asked before connecting

streamsNeeded.name: Connect Facebook And Pick A Year

customerJourneyStories.name: From the Instagram dead end to a shelf of Facebook years
customerJourneyStories.summary: A retired teacher in Ohio, 61, who had printed two Instagram years with PastBook and lost that source when Instagram discontinued third-party access, rediscovers PastBook through the Facebook Photo Books flow, tests it on 2016 and ends up printing every year since 2009.

stages.narrative: Facebook shows her a memory from 2016, a beach week with all three grandchildren, and she realises that fifteen years of family photos exist only on Facebook. Her earlier attempt to keep printing Instagram years had ended with the notice that Instagram no longer supports third-party photo products, and she has not printed anything since.

Her sister posts a photo of a small hardcover with the year 2019 on the spine and says it took one click from Facebook. Searching for it, she lands on pastbook.com, sees the Facebook Photo Books page with albums, timeline pictures and profile photos being turned into a book, and recognises the company from her Instagram books.

She reads the help center article about the Facebook permission screen and the Instagram notice, which tells her honestly what changed and what still works. She checks Trustpilot, 4.5 from 35,837 reviews with PastBook replying under the negative ones, compares USD 19.99 for 24 pages with a Shutterfly book she once paid twice as much for, and decides that the free preview means she risks nothing.

She logs in with Facebook, picks 2016 and watches the book build in under a minute with the captions she wrote at the time. She changes the cover to the beach photo, applies the code from the welcome e-mail and orders the small hardcover; it arrives in six business days and the grandchildren's names are printed under the right faces.

Over the following months she orders 2015, then 2017, waiting for each promotion e-mail before she clicks. Facebook stays connected in her account, so each new year starts at the year picker. When 2011 comes out at 58 pages she asks support on WhatsApp whether the hardcover is included and gets an answer the same evening.

By the next January she owns every year from 2009 to 2025 in the same size, and the yearbook reminder that names the missing years now has nothing left to name except the new one. She stays because the shelf only lines up if the next book comes from the same place, and because PastBook told her the truth when Instagram closed; she leaves a five-star Trustpilot review that mentions exactly that.

customerJourneyStories.name: Gifting the year the first grandchild was born
customerJourneyStories.summary: A grandmother in Melbourne, 66, who printed her Facebook 2012, the year her first grandchild was born, finds out how reorders and extra copies work when her daughter in the UK and her son in Canada both ask for the same book, and becomes the family's archivist.

stages.narrative: At a family video call her daughter in London holds up the phone to the 2012 book on the coffee table and asks for one of her own; her son in Toronto wants one too. The grandmother made that book eight months ago and cannot remember how, and is worried about doing it all again from Facebook.

She goes back to pastbook.com, logs in and finds the 2012 book in her account with its format and 48 pages, plus a note that 2013 and 2014 are still missing. The Year in Review e-mail that week mentions gift copies and shipping to 150+ countries.

She compares having the book reprinted locally in Australia and posting it herself with PastBook shipping a copy to each address, and checks the delivery windows: 4 to 5 business days in the UK, 5 to 10 in Canada, prices in GBP and CAD. The promotion covers reorders, which settles it.

She orders two copies of 2012 to two countries in one checkout, upgrades her daughter's to the large hardcover, and follows both parcels from the same order page. The London copy arrives first and the photo of the book on her daughter's shelf arrives on the family chat before the Toronto tracking says delivered.

Her children now send her their own Facebook years to print, and she orders 2013 and 2014 for herself when the January reminder arrives. She has become the person in the family who knows which years exist, in which size and who has which copy, all visible in her order history.

She keeps ordering from PastBook because the family's books must match across three countries, the reorder starts from the finished book instead of from Facebook, and every parcel so far has arrived inside the window PastBook published. When her son asks whether the photos are safe, she forwards the help center article she read herself.

customers.name: Seasonal Gift Giver
customers.description: A daughter, son or partner between 30 and 55, mostly in the United States, who buys PastBook products as presents rather than for themselves: a Year in Review book of the grandchildren for the parents at Christmas, a wall calendar for the grandparents' kitchen, a rolled poster of the wedding for a partner's birthday, or a gift card when the photos live on someone else's phone. Orders are decided by a date, Christmas, Mother's Day or a birthday, and by a discount or free hardcover upgrade that arrives at the right moment, so the same person may spend USD 34.99 on a large hardcover in November and USD 24.99 on a small calendar in April. Cares most that the parcel arrives before the occasion, that the published delivery windows are honest and that tracking works, because a late gift is worse than no gift.
careAbout: A clear order-by date per country for Christmas and Mother's Day, worked back from production time plus the published delivery window, for example 4 to 8 business days in the United States
A gift that looks personal without an afternoon of design: the Year in Review book or calendar built in under 60 seconds from the phone, with a dedication on the cover
Choosing the right product and size for the recipient, from the small hardcover at USD 19.99 to the large calendar at USD 34.99 or a rolled poster at USD 39.99, with the price known before checkout
Discounts and free-shipping upgrades that land in time for the occasion, and a promo code that works on the whole basket, including calendars and posters
Tracking for a parcel that ships to the recipient's address rather than their own, with a warning early enough to reorder or send a gift card instead
A fallback when there are no photos: a gift card in the recipient's currency or an album the family can fill together
winsThem: PastBook in the GQ gift guide and featured in the App Store in the run-up to the holidays, with the Year in Review campaign showing the book being built in seconds

jobsToBeDone.name: Get a personalised gift delivered before the date
jobsToBeDone.whatItIs: Turn a year of family photos into a printed present that reaches the recipient, often at another address, before Christmas, Mother's Day or a birthday. The job covers knowing the last safe order date for the recipient's country, building the Year in Review book or calendar from the phone in a minute, adding a dedication, paying with the seasonal discount, shipping to the recipient and watching the tracking until it is delivered.
jobsToBeDone.outcome: The gift is ordered before the published order-by date, produced within the promised production time, delivered to the recipient's address inside the published window for that country and before the occasion, and the giver never has to explain a missing present.

steps.description: From the phone camera roll by date or album, from a Facebook year, or from a shared family album, the giver pulls the photos of the grandchildren or of the couple that the recipient will want to see, without sorting through thousands of screenshots.

streamsNeeded.name: Import Photos From Phone And Cloud
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Imports the camera roll by date, album or Yearbook mode and from Dropbox or Google Drive, with timestamps that make a Year in Review possible.

streamsNeeded.name: Connect Facebook And Pick A Year
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Offers the recipient's or the giver's Facebook year as an alternative source when the phone has too few photos.

steps.step: Let the engine make the Year in Review in a minute
steps.description: The curation engine drops duplicates and blurry shots, groups the year into moments and lays out the book or calendar with dates, so the giver sees a finished present in under 60 seconds and shares the highlight video with a sibling to check nobody is missing.

streamsNeeded.name: Curate The Best Photos With Ai
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Selects the best photos of the year and groups them into moments so that the gift shows a whole year, not a hundred near-duplicates.

streamsNeeded.name: Auto Design The Book And Preview
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Produces the Year in Review book or calendar preview and the shareable highlight video the giver uses to get a second opinion.

steps.step: Add a dedication and the right cover
steps.description: A cover photo of the grandparents with the children, a quote on the first page and the year on the spine make it a present. The giver wants to do this in a few taps and not learn a layout tool on a December evening.

streamsNeeded.name: Edit And Personalise The Book
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Lets the giver choose the cover photo, theme colours, a quote and a back-cover photo without touching the automatic layout.

steps.step: Pay with the promotion and ship to the recipient
steps.description: The giver picks the format, applies the holiday code or free hardcover upgrade, enters the recipient's address and pays with a card or PayPal, seeing the delivery estimate for that address before confirming.

streamsNeeded.name: Choose Format Price And Checkout
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Applies the promo code or free upgrade, prices the basket in the giver's currency and takes the recipient's shipping address and the payment.

steps.step: Track the parcel and step in if it slips
steps.description: Because the parcel goes to someone else's door, the giver watches the tracking and wants a warning early enough to reorder, send a gift card or tell the recipient, and a fast reprint if the gift arrives damaged.

streamsNeeded.name: Produce Ship And Track The Order
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Produces the order at the partner facility nearest the recipient, ships it and provides tracking with delivery estimates.

streamsNeeded.name: Resolve Support Requests And Reprints
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Handles address changes, late-parcel questions and reprints or refunds 24/7 on WhatsApp, e-mail and chat.

jobsToBeDone.name: Pick the right product, size and price for the recipient
jobsToBeDone.whatItIs: Choose, for each person on the list, the PastBook product that fits them and the budget: a large hardcover for the parents, a wall calendar for the grandparents' kitchen, a folded or rolled poster for a partner, gift cards for those with their own photos. The job includes understanding cover rules and page-count pricing, using the promotion on the whole basket and bundling several products into one order.
jobsToBeDone.outcome: Every recipient gets a product they will actually use, the giver knows the full price including extra pages and shipping before checkout, the promotion applies to every item in the basket and the whole order ships together on time.

steps.step: Match the product to the person
steps.description: A grandmother who still writes on a paper calendar gets the 8 x 11.7 inch wall calendar at USD 24.99, a father who likes big photos gets the large 12 x 8.5 inch hardcover at USD 34.99, a partner gets the rolled poster at USD 39.99 for the living room.

streamsNeeded.name: Choose Format Price And Checkout
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Presents books, calendars and posters with sizes and prices side by side so the giver can match a product to each recipient.

steps.step: Understand what the page count does to cover and price
steps.description: Up to 16 pages is softcover, 18 to 26 pages a choice, 27 to 300 pages hardcover by default; every page above 24 costs USD 0.40 small or USD 0.55 large. The giver wants this visible while adding or removing photos, not at the last screen.

streamsNeeded.name: Choose Format Price And Checkout
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Applies the cover rules by page count and shows the running price as the page count changes.

streamsNeeded.name: Edit And Personalise The Book
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Lets the giver remove or add photos to land on the page count and cover they want to pay for.

steps.step: Use the promotion on everything in the basket
steps.description: The holiday code or free hardcover upgrade must work on the book, the calendar and the poster in the same order, in the giver's currency, and the giver wants to know the discount is the best one available this week.

streamsNeeded.name: Run Seasonal Campaigns And Promotions
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Runs the seasonal discounts, free-shipping and upgrade offers and states which products they cover.

streamsNeeded.name: Choose Format Price And Checkout
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Applies codes and gift cards across the basket and shows the discounted total before payment.

steps.step: Check the gift through the recipient's eyes
steps.description: The giver previews the calendar month by month to see that the grandparents' birthdays fall on months with their photos, and sends the highlight video to a sibling to confirm the choice before paying.

streamsNeeded.name: Auto Design The Book And Preview
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Shows the full preview of each product for free and produces the highlight video the giver shares for a second opinion.

steps.step: Order several products for several people at once
steps.description: One checkout with a book, two calendars and a poster to two addresses, knowing that the order ships on the longest production time and that each parcel has its own tracking.

streamsNeeded.name: Choose Format Price And Checkout
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Handles multi-product, multi-address orders in one checkout with shipping per destination.

streamsNeeded.name: Render Print Ready Files And Route To A Printer
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Renders print-ready files for each product and routes the pieces to the partner facilities that can produce them together on time.

jobsToBeDone.name: Give when I have no photos: gift cards and shared albums
jobsToBeDone.whatItIs: Give a PastBook present when the photos are on someone else's phone: a gift card so the new parents make their own first-year book, or an album the family fills together before the giver orders the book. The job includes buying the card in the right currency, helping a less technical recipient install the app and redeem it, and coming back next year.
jobsToBeDone.outcome: The gift card is bought and delivered before the occasion, redeemed by the recipient for a product they chose themselves, and the giver is reminded in time for the next occasion, so a present without photos still ends as a printed book.

steps.step: Buy a gift card in the recipient's currency
steps.description: The giver picks a gift card that covers a small hardcover or a calendar in the recipient's currency, USD, GBP, EUR or AUD, and has it delivered by e-mail in time for the date.

streamsNeeded.name: Choose Format Price And Checkout
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Sells gift cards in the seven currencies and delivers the code in time for the occasion.

streamsNeeded.name: Run Seasonal Campaigns And Promotions
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Promotes gift cards as the last-minute option after the physical order-by date has passed.

steps.step: Collect the photos the family holds
steps.description: For a first-year book of a nephew, the giver asks the parents to share an album from their phone or a Google Drive folder, so the photos exist in one place before anyone builds a book.

streamsNeeded.name: Import Photos From Phone And Cloud
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Imports a shared phone album or a Dropbox or Google Drive folder that the family has filled together.

steps.step: Help the recipient install the app and redeem
steps.description: A grandparent who receives a gift card needs to find the PastBook app, allow photo access and enter the code. The giver wants a link that does all three and a helpline that answers if it goes wrong.

streamsNeeded.name: Discover And Install The App
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Gets the recipient from the gift card e-mail to an installed app with photo-library permission granted.

streamsNeeded.name: Resolve Support Requests And Reprints
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Helps a less technical recipient redeem the card and place the first order through chat or WhatsApp.

steps.step: Come back for the next occasion
steps.description: Once the recipient has made a book, the giver wants a reminder before the next Mother's Day or Christmas, with the recipient's addresses saved and the products they liked remembered.

streamsNeeded.name: Retain Customers With Yearbooks And Reminders
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Sends occasion reminders to the giver with saved recipients and the products ordered last time, and prompts a rating after delivery.

customerJourneyStories.name: A Year in Review for the grandparents, ordered on 3 December
customerJourneyStories.summary: A father of two in Texas, 38, whose parents live in Florida, replaces the annual framed print with a PastBook Year in Review book and a calendar, learns to trust the order-by date, and turns it into the family's fixed Christmas present.

stages.narrative: It is the first weekend of December and the family chat asks what the grandparents get this year; last year's framed print took three weeks and arrived after Christmas. His phone holds 9,000 photos of the children from the year and no time to sort them.

The PastBook app appears in an App Store holiday feature and in a paid Instagram ad for the Year in Review book, and a colleague mentions the GQ gift guide listing. He installs the app because the ad promised a book in seconds rather than a design tool.

He checks the pricing and shipping page, sees that US delivery is 4 to 8 business days after production and that the campaign banner shows the last order date for Christmas. He compares the USD 34.99 large hardcover with a Shutterfly promotion, reads Trustpilot reviews from other gift givers about pre-Christmas delivery, and the free hardcover upgrade on a second copy settles it.

Yearbook mode builds the book from the year's camera roll in under a minute; he swaps the cover to the grandparents with both kids, adds a dedication, orders a copy for each set of grandparents and a small calendar, and follows the tracking to Florida. The parcel arrives on 15 December, ten days before Christmas.

In April the app reminds him of Mother's Day with a calendar offer, in the summer he orders a rolled poster of the beach trip for his wife's birthday, and his order history keeps the grandparents' addresses so a reorder takes two minutes.

The following November a reminder arrives before he has thought about presents, with last year's book as the starting point and the order-by date for Florida. He stays because the one time a calendar arrived creased, support replaced it within the week over WhatsApp, and because the grandparents now expect the next volume.

customerJourneyStories.name: A gift card and a shared album for a first-year book
customerJourneyStories.summary: A 29-year-old in London wants to give her brother and his partner a book of their baby's first year, has none of the photos herself, and discovers that a PastBook gift card plus a shared album lets the parents make the book they want, delivered within the UK's 4 to 5 business days.

stages.narrative: Her nephew turns one in three weeks and the parents have 4,000 photos on two phones and no printed picture of him. She wants to give something personal but cannot make a book from photos she does not have.

A friend's Instagram story shows a PastBook highlight video of her own baby book; the pastbook.com pricing page lists gift cards next to books, calendars and posters and the delivery window for the UK.

She weighs a gift card against sending the parents a link to make the book and paying afterwards, checks that a gift card in GBP covers the small hardcover at GBP 16.99 plus extra pages, and reads in the help center how redemption works. The card is safer than guessing which photos the parents want.

She buys the gift card in GBP, sends it with a note for the birthday, and creates a shared album the parents fill with 300 favourites. The parents install the app from the gift card e-mail, redeem the code and order a 40-page hardcover that arrives in four business days.

The parents keep the app and order a second copy for the other grandparents; she sends a gift card again for Christmas and a calendar for her own mother from the same shared album, using the promo code from the seasonal e-mail.

She keeps choosing PastBook for family occasions because the gift card removed the risk of picking the wrong photos, the parents have since become PastBook customers themselves, and the reminder before her nephew's second birthday lands with the shared album still there to build the next book.

top.name: Gifts delivered before the occasion
top.description: Share of gift orders with a stated occasion date, Christmas, Mother's Day or a birthday, that were delivered to the recipient before that date. Modeled seed value, not an official PastBook figure: about 78 percent of gift orders are placed with enough lead time and almost all of those arrive in time, while roughly 63 percent of the rush orders placed in the last seven days still make it, which gives about 91 percent overall.

branches.name: Ordered in time and delivered on time
branches.description: Whether the giver orders before the last safe date and whether production and carriers keep the published windows in the peak season.

children.name: On-time delivery rate in peak season
children.description: Share of orders placed between 1 November and 24 December that are delivered within the published production plus delivery window for the destination country.

children.name: Peak orders handed to the carrier within production SLA
children.description: Share of peak-season orders that partner facilities produce and hand to the carrier within the agreed production time.

children.name: Peak parcels delivered within the published carrier window
children.description: Share of peak-season parcels delivered by the carrier within the published window for the country, for example 4 to 8 business days in the United States.

children.name: Gift orders placed with enough lead time
children.description: Share of gift orders placed on or before the published order-by date for the occasion and destination country.

children.name: Gift givers who saw the order-by date before checkout
children.description: Share of gift orders where the giver was shown the order-by date for the recipient's country in the campaign, app or checkout before paying.

children.name: Rush orders placed inside the last seven days before the occasion
children.description: Share of gift orders placed within seven days of the occasion, the complement of orders placed in time.

branches.name: The right gift, tracked and worry-free
branches.description: Whether gift cards actually turn into printed products and whether the giver has to contact support about a parcel going to someone else's door.

children.name: Gift card redemption rate
children.description: Share of gift cards sold that are redeemed for a product within twelve months.

children.name: Gift cards redeemed within 90 days of purchase
children.description: Share of gift cards redeemed within 90 days, typically before the occasion after the one they were bought for.

children.name: Redeemed gift cards turned into a delivered product
children.description: Share of redeemed gift cards where the recipient completes an order that is delivered, rather than stopping at a preview.

children.name: Gift orders with a tracking or delivery support contact
children.description: Share of gift orders that generate at least one support contact about tracking, address, delay or damage.

children.name: Gift shipments with the tracking link opened by the giver
children.description: Share of gift shipments whose tracking link the giver opens at least once, a proxy for proactive tracking replacing a support question.

children.name: Gift orders reprinted or refunded for late or damaged delivery
children.description: Share of gift orders that end in a reprint or refund because the parcel arrived late, damaged or at the wrong address.

top.name: Annual gross margin from gift orders
top.description: Retail revenue from gift orders, Year in Review books, calendars, posters and gift cards, minus partner print, shipping, discount, payment and reprint cost. Modeled seed value, not an official PastBook figure: about 260,000 gift orders at USD 41 average order value and USD 20 gross margin per order, with 58 percent of the orders in the fourth quarter.

branches.name: Seasonal gift order volume and value
branches.description: How many gift orders arrive across Christmas, Mother's Day and birthdays and how much each basket is worth with calendars, posters and multiple copies.

children.name: Gift orders per year
children.description: Paid orders per year shipped to an address other than the buyer's or flagged as a gift, including gift card purchases.

children.name: Gift orders in the fourth quarter
children.description: Share of gift orders placed between 1 October and 31 December; a lower share means Mother's Day and birthdays carry more of the year.

children.name: Year in Review books ordered as gifts
children.description: Year in Review photo books per year shipped as gifts, the largest single gift product.

children.name: Average gift order value
children.description: Average paid amount per gift order after discounts, across books from USD 19.99, calendars at USD 24.99 and 34.99 and posters at USD 29.99 and 39.99.

children.name: Multi-product gift orders
children.description: Share of gift orders containing more than one product or copy, for example a book plus a calendar or copies for two sets of grandparents.

children.name: Calendar and poster share of gift orders
children.description: Share of gift orders that include a wall calendar or a poster.

branches.name: Margin discipline in the gifting season
branches.description: What each gift order earns after print, shipping, discounts and free upgrades, and what a new gift giver costs to acquire in the most expensive advertising quarter.

children.name: Gross margin per gift order
children.description: Average gift order value minus print and shipping cost and minus discount, payment and reprint cost: 41 - 17.5 - 3.5 = 20.

children.name: Print and shipping cost per gift order
children.description: Partner print and carrier cost per gift order, higher than a single book because of calendars, posters and multiple copies.

children.name: Discount, free-upgrade and reprint cost per gift order
children.description: Cost of promo discounts, free hardcover upgrades and free shipping offers, payment fees and reprints per gift order.

children.name: Acquisition cost per new gift giver in the fourth quarter
children.description: Paid marketing cost per first-time gift buyer acquired between 1 October and 31 December, when ad auctions are most expensive.

children.name: New gift givers acquired through paid channels in the fourth quarter
children.description: Share of new fourth-quarter gift buyers attributed to paid social and search rather than App Store featuring, gift guides, referrals or reminders.

children.name: Return on ad spend of the Year in Review campaign
children.description: Gift order revenue attributed to the Year in Review campaign divided by its paid media spend.

productStrategy.vision: Make PastBook the gift that always arrives: a Year in Review book, calendar or poster built from the phone in a minute, priced and discounted transparently, with an order-by date per country the giver can trust and a gift card for every occasion where the photos belong to someone else.

year1.focus: Make the Christmas peak reliable: publish order-by dates per country, keep partner production and carriers inside the published windows in November and December, and stop rush orders from becoming late gifts and reprints.
year1.productTheme: Ordered in time, delivered before the date

supporting: On-time delivery rate in peak season
Gift givers who saw the order-by date before checkout

revenueStreams: Year in Review books at USD 19.99 small and USD 34.99 large for 24 pages, sold as gifts
Wall calendars at USD 24.99 and USD 34.99 and posters at USD 29.99 and USD 39.99
supporting: Gift orders per year
Gross margin per gift order

milestones: Show the last order date for Christmas and Mother's Day per destination country in the app, on the campaign pages and at checkout
Agree peak production SLAs and redundant capacity with partner facilities in the United States, the United Kingdom and the EU before the fourth quarter
Send proactive tracking and delay notices to gift givers so that a slipping parcel is known before the occasion, not after

year3.focus: Spread gifting across the year and deepen the basket: occasion reminders with saved recipients, calendars and posters alongside the book, and gift cards that are redeemed rather than forgotten, so the fourth quarter carries a smaller share of the load.
year3.productTheme: Every occasion, every recipient, one order

supporting: Gift card redemption rate
Gift orders placed with enough lead time

businessKPI.northStar: Annual gross margin from gift orders
revenueStreams: Multi-product gift baskets of books, calendars and posters shipped to several addresses
Mother's Day and birthday gifting outside the fourth quarter
Gift cards redeemed for a first book by new households
supporting: Multi-product gift orders
Gift orders in the fourth quarter

milestones: Launch occasion reminders with saved recipients, their addresses and the products ordered last time, starting with Mother's Day and birthdays
Offer multi-address checkout so that copies for several grandparents ship in one order with tracking per parcel
Redesign the gift card e-mail so that the recipient installs the app and builds a first book within 90 days

year5.focus: Be the default personalised gift in 150+ countries: any photo stream turned into a printed present, produced locally near the recipient, with sustainability and on-time delivery as the brand promise and paid acquisition replaced largely by reminders, referrals and redeemed gift cards.
year5.productTheme: The gift that always arrives, anywhere

supporting: Gift orders with a tracking or delivery support contact
Gift orders reprinted or refunded for late or damaged delivery

Family gifting circles where gift cards and shared albums bring new households in
Premium large-format and multi-copy gift baskets

Return on ad spend of the Year in Review campaign

milestones: Produce gift orders in the recipient's country for the large majority of destinations, with FSC paper and a published delivery window for each
Bring gift-related support contacts below one in twenty orders through proactive tracking, delay notices and self-service address changes
